title: Distance to bank as IV for savings rate

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We employ the Instrumental Variable (IV) method, using distance to the nearest bank branch (z) as the instrument for having a bank account (x). The first stage equation models the relationship between z and x, where we expect a negative coefficient, indicating that households closer to a bank branch are more likely to have an account. The second stage equation models the relationship between x and the monthly savings (y). The key assumptions for the IV method are: (i) the instrument (z) is relevant, i.e., it affects the endogenous variable (x); (ii) the instrument satisfies the exclusion restriction, i.e., it affects the outcome variable (y) only through its effect on the endogenous variable (x); and (iii) the instrument is exogenous, i.e., it is not correlated with the error term in the second stage equation.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(AER)
library(readr)

# Read the CSV file
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s20_data.csv")

# First stage: distance -> account ownership
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
summary(first_stage)

# Second stage: account ownership -> savings
second_stage <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
summary(second_stage)

# IV regression
ivRegression <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
summary(ivRegression)

# Basic robustness checks: check for overidentifying restrictions
# (not applicable here since we have only one instrument)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the instrument (distance to the nearest bank branch) to have a negative effect on having a bank account in the first stage, as households closer to a bank branch are more likely to have an account. In the second stage, we expect the coefficient on having a bank account to be positive, indicating that households with a bank account tend to have higher savings rates. The magnitude of this effect is expected to be moderate, given that having a bank account can facilitate savings by providing a secure and convenient way to store money. However, the exact magnitude will depend on various factors, including income, education, and other household characteristics.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: branch distance; first stage: distance → account ownership (negative)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Bank account ownership significantly increases savings
_ground_truth.main_effect: Having an account increases monthly savings by ~40% (IV estimate)
